source_text: Et illud propter hoc relinquet homo patrem et matrem et adhaerebit uxori suae, et erunt duo in carne una ut exprimere fidem operum, propheta prope periculum pudoris accessit
pass_a_gloss: And that: for this a man will leave father and mother and will cling to his wife, and they will be two in one flesh. And that he might express the faith of the works, the prophet approached near the danger of modesty.
pass_b_english: “For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and cling to his wife, and the two will be one flesh” (Genesis 2:24).
To state faithfully how these works take place, the prophet came close to risking modesty.

choices.why: Opening fides promissionis is the pledge of a promise, not the theological virtue.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

bible_refs.note: Linked from Julian's wording or a clear allusion in the excerpt.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, De nuptiis et concupiscentia 2 / On Marriage and Concupiscence); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
